title: Commands
description: Tell someone what to do or not to do, with or without pronouns.
rule: The imperative has three forms, taken from the present without the subject: tu, nous and vous (finis, finissons, finissez). In the tu form, -er verbs and aller drop the final s (parle, va), as do verbs like ouvrir whose tu form ends in -es (ouvre), but they keep it before y or en (vas-y, manges-en). Être, avoir and savoir are irregular: sois, soyons, soyez; aie, ayons, ayez; sache, sachons, sachez. In the negative, ne and pas surround the verb: ne parle pas, ne sortez pas. In the affirmative, object and reflexive pronouns follow the verb with a hyphen, and me and te become moi and toi: prends-le, donne-moi le sel, lève-toi. With two pronouns, le, la or les comes first: donne-le-moi. In the negative, the pronouns stay before the verb: ne le prends pas, ne te lève pas.
example: Parle plus lentement, s’il te plaît. · Asseyez-vous. · Ne le mange pas !
aside: The nous form is a suggestion rather than an order: allons-y means let’s go.

alternatives.message: Parles is the present. In the imperative, -er verbs drop the final s of the tu form.

exercises.hint: Start from tu parles and remove the subject. -er verbs lose one more letter.
exercises.feedback: The tu imperative of an -er verb has no final s.
exercises.explanation: Tu parles becomes parle: -er verbs drop the s in the tu command.

exercises.instruction: Write manger as a command to a friend (tu form).

alternatives.message: Manges is the present. In the imperative, -er verbs drop the final s of the tu form.

exercises.hint: Take tu manges, remove tu, and think about the last letter.
exercises.feedback: An -er verb has no final s in the tu command.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of manger is mange, without s.

exercises.hint: S’il te plaît shows this is a tu command, and fermer is an -er verb.
exercises.feedback: Look for the tu command of an -er verb.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of fermer is ferme, with no s.

exercises.hint: Écouter is an -er verb. Look at the last letter of the verb.
exercises.feedback: The verb still has the ending of the present tense.
exercises.explanation: In the tu command, -er verbs drop the s: écoute.

alternatives.message: That is a casual suggestion. Here, use the nous form of the imperative, without a subject.

exercises.hint: Let’s is the nous command: the nous form without nous.
exercises.feedback: Use the nous form of manger, without the subject.
exercises.explanation: Let’s eat is the nous command mangeons. Manger keeps its e before -ons.

answers: Parle plus fort, s’il te plaît.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of parler. Only one is a command.
exercises.feedback: The tu command of an -er verb has no final s.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of parler is parle, without s.

exercises.hint: Take the nous form of the present and remove nous.
exercises.feedback: The nous command is the nous present form without the subject.
exercises.explanation: Nous finissons becomes finissons.

alternatives.message: Only -er verbs and aller drop the s. Prendre keeps the tu form of the present: prends.

exercises.hint: Prendre is not an -er verb, so its tu form stays as in the present.
exercises.feedback: Keep the tu present form of prendre, without tu.
exercises.explanation: Tu prends becomes prends. Only -er verbs and aller drop the s.

exercises.instruction: Write faire as a command (vous form).
exercises.hint: Take the vous form of faire in the present and remove vous.
exercises.feedback: The vous form of faire is irregular in the present, and the command keeps it.
exercises.explanation: Vous faites becomes faites.

exercises.hint: You are speaking to several children.
exercises.feedback: Speaking to several people calls for the vous command.
exercises.explanation: To several people, the command of venir is venez.

exercises.instruction: Turn this into a command: keep the tu form and drop the subject.
exercises.hint: Attendre is not an -er verb, so the verb itself does not change.
exercises.feedback: Remove tu and keep attends as it is.
exercises.explanation: Tu attends becomes attends: only -er verbs and aller drop the s.

exercises.hint: Boire is irregular. Use its tu present form without tu.
exercises.feedback: Use the tu command of boire and the partitive for some water.
exercises.explanation: Tu bois becomes bois; some water is de l’eau.

alternatives.message: Vas is the present. Aller drops the s in the tu command, except before y or en.

exercises.hint: Aller behaves like an -er verb in the tu command.
exercises.feedback: The tu command of aller has no s here.
exercises.explanation: Tu vas becomes va, like the -er verbs.

exercises.source: ____ à la boulangerie, s’il te plaît.
exercises.hint: This is a tu command, and no y or en follows the verb.
exercises.feedback: Aller drops the s in the tu command.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of aller is va. The s only comes back before y or en.

exercises.hint: Before en, the tu command gets back a letter. Pronouns also need a hyphen.
exercises.feedback: Think about the s before en and the hyphen.
exercises.explanation: Before en, the s returns for the sound: manges-en.

exercises.instruction: Write aller in the tu imperative. Write only the missing word.
exercises.source: Le parc est ouvert : ____-y avec ton frère !

alternatives.message: Right form, but -y is already in the sentence. Write only the missing word.
Aller drops the s in the tu command, but the s comes back before y.

exercises.hint: The word after the blank is y.
exercises.feedback: Before y, the tu command of aller keeps a letter it usually loses.
exercises.explanation: Before y, the s returns: vas-y.

alternatives.message: Before y, the tu command of aller takes back its s: vas-y.
In the affirmative imperative, the pronoun is joined to the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.hint: Y goes after the verb, and the verb changes slightly before it.
exercises.feedback: Before y, the s comes back, and a hyphen joins the words.
exercises.explanation: Au marché becomes y after the verb, and va becomes vas before y: vas-y.

exercises.hint: Look at the verb before y.
exercises.feedback: Before y, the tu command of aller keeps its s.
exercises.explanation: Va becomes vas before y: vas-y.

exercises.source: Talk to your father about it (to a friend).
exercises.hint: Before en, the tu command of an -er verb changes.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is missing a letter that returns before en.
exercises.explanation: Before en, the s returns: parles-en.

exercises.hint: Être does not take its imperative from the present.
exercises.feedback: The imperative of être is irregular.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of être is sois.

alternatives.message: Avez is the present. The imperative of avoir is irregular.

exercises.hint: Avoir does not take its imperative from the present.
exercises.feedback: The imperative of avoir is irregular.
exercises.explanation: The vous command of avoir is ayez.

exercises.hint: Avoir is irregular in the imperative, and you are speaking to several children.
exercises.feedback: Use the irregular vous command of avoir.
exercises.explanation: To several people: n’ayez pas peur. Aie is the tu form.

exercises.hint: Être is irregular in the imperative, and sages is plural.
exercises.feedback: Use the irregular vous command of être.
exercises.explanation: To several people, the command of être is soyez.

exercises.instruction: Write savoir as a command to a friend (tu form).
exercises.source: ____ que je suis toujours là pour toi.

alternatives.message: Sais is the present. The imperative of savoir is irregular.

exercises.hint: Savoir has an irregular imperative, like être and avoir.
exercises.feedback: The tu command of savoir is not taken from the present.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of savoir is sache.

exercises.hint: Look at the last letter of the verb.
exercises.feedback: The tu command of être ends in s.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of être is sois. Soit is a different form.

exercises.hint: Être has an irregular imperative. On time is à l’heure.
exercises.feedback: Use the irregular vous command of être.
exercises.explanation: The vous command of être is soyez: soyez à l’heure.

exercises.source: Have confidence in yourself (to a friend).
exercises.hint: Avoir has an irregular tu command. One tile is a wrong form.
exercises.feedback: The tu command of avoir has no s.
exercises.explanation: The tu command of avoir is aie.

exercises.hint: Ne and pas go around the verb, as in a normal sentence.
exercises.feedback: Put ne before the verb and pas after it.
exercises.explanation: In a negative command, ne and pas surround the verb: ne mange pas.

exercises.hint: Speaking to Paul is a tu command. Courir is not an -er verb.
exercises.feedback: Use the tu present form of courir without tu.
exercises.explanation: Tu cours becomes cours: ne cours pas.

exercises.instruction: Write attendre as a nous command.
exercises.source: N’____ pas le bus : il est toujours en retard.
exercises.hint: Take the nous present form and remove nous.
exercises.feedback: The nous command sits between n’ and pas.
exercises.explanation: Nous attendons becomes attendons: n’attendons pas.

exercises.source: Don’t touch the cake (to a friend).

alternatives.message: That is casual speech. In standard written French, keep ne before the verb.
That is casual speech. In standard written French, keep ne before the verb.

exercises.hint: Ne and pas go around the verb. Toucher is an -er verb.
exercises.feedback: Put ne before the tu command and pas after it.
exercises.explanation: Ne touche pas surrounds the verb; -er verbs have no s in the tu command.

exercises.hint: Look at where pas is.
exercises.feedback: Pas must come straight after the verb.
exercises.explanation: Ne and pas surround the verb: ne fermez pas la porte.

exercises.source: Don’t go out tonight (to several people).
exercises.hint: Choose the vous command, then place ne and pas around it.
exercises.feedback: Pick the vous command form of sortir.
exercises.explanation: Ne and pas surround the vous command sortez.

alternatives.message: After the verb, te becomes toi: lève-toi.
In the affirmative imperative, the pronoun is joined to the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.hint: The pronoun goes after the verb in an affirmative command, and te changes.
exercises.feedback: Put the pronoun after the verb with a hyphen, in its stressed form.
exercises.explanation: Tu te lèves becomes lève-toi: the pronoun follows, and te becomes toi.

alternatives.message: In the affirmative imperative, the pronoun is joined to the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.hint: Take vous vous asseyez and move the pronoun after the verb.
exercises.feedback: The reflexive pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen.
exercises.explanation: Vous vous asseyez becomes asseyez-vous (assoyez-vous is the less common variant).

exercises.hint: In an affirmative command, the pronoun follows the verb and te changes form.
exercises.feedback: Check where the pronoun goes, its form, and the -er ending.
exercises.explanation: Réveille-toi: the pronoun follows with a hyphen, te becomes toi, and the -er verb has no s.

exercises.hint: In the negative, the pronoun goes back before the verb.
exercises.feedback: In a negative command, the reflexive pronoun is te and comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Lève-toi becomes ne te lève pas: te goes before the verb, inside ne…pas.

exercises.explanation: In the negative, the pronoun stays in front: ne te couche pas.

alternatives.message: In the affirmative imperative, the pronoun is joined to the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.hint: Use the nous command and put the pronoun after the verb.
exercises.feedback: The reflexive pronoun follows the nous command with a hyphen.
exercises.explanation: Nous nous dépêchons becomes dépêchons-nous.

exercises.instruction: Write se laver as a vous command, with its pronoun.

alternatives.message: In the affirmative imperative, the pronoun is joined to the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.feedback: Check the pronoun’s position and form, and the -er ending.
exercises.explanation: Donne-moi: the pronoun follows, me becomes moi, and the -er verb has no s.

exercises.feedback: Put la after the verb with a hyphen; the -er verb has no s.
exercises.explanation: Tu appelles becomes appelle, and la follows: appelle-la.

exercises.hint: Look at the pronoun after the verb.
exercises.feedback: After the verb, me takes its stressed form.
exercises.explanation: In an affirmative command, me becomes moi: aide-moi.
